newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar at two-month high against softer mark.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar at two-month high against softer mark.

text.p: The dollar hit a two-month peak against the mark in Europe on Friday and volatile London shares retreated sharply from an opening rally which took them to a new record high.
A weaker mark saw the dollar rise to a morning high of 1.5186 marks before some profit-taking dulled its advance.

Dealers said most activity had been between the mark and other European currencies, particularly the french franc, which was being bought heavily against the mark following the publication of the French budget. Generally speaking, dealers said, interest rate jitters were still overhanging the currency markets with the main topic of conversation being next week's U.S. rate-setting Federal Open Markets Committee meeting. Many analysts expect a 25 basis point (quarter percent) rise in the Fed funds rate.
Leading British and German shares opened higher on Friday -- London breaking records -- ignoring another choppy day on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Average closed down again.
But British stocks had retreated into negative territory by late morning after their brief rally, which traders said was related to futures and options.

The quarterly futures and options expiry is important because market players have to decide whether to take any profits or losses on their positions or to "roll over," or take new positions, in the next contract period.

The expiry is often associated with unsually high levels of market volatility as traders and investors bet on market moves through the next three months, using derivatives which often set the pace for the rest of the stock market.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index had jumped to a new best of 3,994.1, a rise of 19.8, beating its previous best of 3,987.7 set on Thursday.

In Frankfurt, German shares were bullish, almost one percent up at midday, holding onto higher levels attained earlier on the knock-on effect from their own futures expiry trade. Dealers said the market was also supported by the firmer dollar, which makes German exports more attractive.
But French shares were at their lows for the day with dealers saying the market was drifting amid lack of consensus over its direction.
The dollar was at 1.5170 marks and 109.80 yen compared with 1.5139 marks and 109.40 yen in Europe late on Thursday.
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 9.2 points at 3,965.1
In Paris, the CAC-40 share was down 8.64 points at 2,073.54
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 21.66 at 2,646.10. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $382.50, compared with its close in London on Thursday of $382.85. Silver was weaker at $4.95.
